titre: Histoire du concept : John Michell, Einstein et la relativité générale
resume: The first person to describe a black hole was John Michell, an English clergyman, in 1783, but his ideas were forgotten until the mathematics existed. In 1915 Einstein's general relativity predicted black holes, the community was divided, but physicists using his equations showed they were theoretically possible.
texte: The first person to describe a black hole was a religious man in England by the name of John Michell in 1783. Michell was considered a brilliant scientist at the time. However, his ideas eventually fell into obscurity since [music] the math and understanding of physics necessary to explain how a black hole works wouldn't be invented for another century and a half. In 1915, when Albert Einstein came up with his theory of general relativity, he predicted [music] the existence of black holes based on the equations that he invented. At this point, the scientific [music] community was divided on whether such a powerful and terrifying source of gravity could actually exist, [music] but as cosmologists and mathematicians began to investigate the universe using Einstein's equations, it became clear that black holes were indeed [music] theoretically possible.
